entries.narrative: MF-030 closes a silent failure of the epic's binding complexity gate. analyze_complexity.py read one .tla file and stopped at EXTENDS, so on the decomposed architecture SKILL.md mandates it scored only the declarations literally present in the analyzed file. The error is never conservative: missing variables only ever shrink the product bound, so the gate failed toward PASS on exactly the shape the skill requires. MF-023 measured External reporting bound = 1 over 2 of 9 variables from this. The fix is a partial module resolver (resolve_module) that follows EXTENDS through the hierarchy and unions VARIABLES, CONSTANTS, and the top-level definitions carrying TypeInvariant/Init/actions, base-first with the extending module overriding inherited names. Standard TLA+ library modules (Naturals, Integers, Reals, Sequences, FiniteSets, Bags, TLC, Json) declare no VARIABLES the bound reads and are skipped rather than resolved to a file. Every construct the resolver cannot model FAILS CLOSED with a named error rather than under-reporting: INSTANCE / named and unnamed instantiation, WITH substitution, and parameterized instantiation via UnsupportedModuleConstructError; LOCAL via the same; and an EXTENDS naming a non-standard module with no findable .tla via UnresolvedExtendsError. analyze() propagates these; run() and gate_report() catch them and fail closed (nonzero / gate FAIL with the reason). This honours references/architecture_tractability.md "No Degenerate Escapes": when a model cannot be resolved, write the failure, not a smaller number. Measured alternatives and the self-scrutiny check: the risk flagged for this ticket was a resolver that appears to work on a model where the extended declarations do not matter to the bound. The regression fixture is deliberately the opposite -- Channel EXTENDS Counter, where the EXTENDED module carries the only bound-bearing variable (tick in 0..3) and the extending module adds only an unconstrained channel variable. Pre-fix the analyzer reports variables= ['emitted'], bound=1, Bump absent; post-fix variables={tick,emitted}, bound=4, Bump present. The number moves 1->4 and the assertions were run against the HEAD analyzer to confirm they fail pre-fix. Shipped example re-measured (examples/distributed_history, External EXTENDS Internal EXTENDS Core, no TypeInvariant so bound is 1 both ways): its verdict stays FAIL but the diagnosis is corrected from a spurious "C2 {responses} touched by 9 actions" (an artifact of seeing only External's 4 variables) to the true "C1 {accounts,carts,orders, responses} touched by 13 actions" over all 10 variables, with named port-crossing actions and modularity 0.000 -> 0.230. That corrected figure is relevant to MF-037 and the ticket-workflow example: any downstream copy of the old 9-action number is stale. Evidence: results/tlc_current.txt, results/shipped_example_external_postfix.txt, results/graph-reports/*.

The recursive-refinement search for a further architectural reduction found none applicable, because the ticket's objective was to STOP the tooling from blocking promotion on complexity, not to reduce complexity. The one measurement-accuracy correction -- the v'=v frame-condition R/W fix -- reduces over-reported coupling in the scanner but does not change this model's own bound or reachable-state count (the model uses UNCHANGED tuples, which were already stripped; the fix matters for models that write explicit frame conditions, e.g. the recorded GodObjectCli probe).

entries.narrative: MF-036 makes the complexity check ADVISORY. A probe built a plain 5-variable, 10-command god-object CLI (recorded under results/probe/GodObjectCli.tla) and ran `analyze complexity`; it HARD-FAILED with "component C1 is touched by 10 actions, exceeding max_component_actions 8" (exit 1). Any program with more than eight commands over shared state failed the same way -- i.e. most real programs. Per owner direction 2026-07-20 and references/architecture_tractability.md ("Advisory, Not Blocking"), complexity is a scanner, not a gate. What changed (scripts only, zero TLA delta): (1) Every complexity threshold breach -- state-space bound, component variables, component actions, and the TLC distinct-states check -- is now an advisory WARNING that names the component/variable/action and RECOMMENDS a concrete move (e.g. "split the densest state <v> into its own component"). `analyze complexity` exits 0 whenever it can analyze the model; it exits nonzero ONLY when it CANNOT analyze it (the MF-030 fail-closed on an unresolved EXTENDS/INSTANCE hierarchy). "I could not measure this" stays an error; "this is complex" is now a finding. (2) Case generation no longer refuses above threshold. `enforce_complexity_gate` became `advise_complexity`: it prints the warnings and proceeds. The `--allow-over-budget` override was removed entirely -- there is no gate left to override. (3) Frame-condition accuracy fix: `v' = v` (the written-out form of UNCHANGED) was counted as a read AND a write, so every variable an action leaves alone showed as coupled to it. It is now stripped. On the GodObjectCli probe this drops the over-reported god-state from all five variables at 10/10 to the real coupling (only the shared `status` at 10/10; the four domain vars at 3/3/2/2), and the R/W interaction graph de-densifies from the complete graph (10 edges) to a star (4 edges). Evidence integrity is untouched: no case is dropped, no effect gap suppressed, no finding silenced. The kill-test mutant inv-SpecUnitTestsRequireAnalyzedGate was kept (its `find` pattern retargeted to the renamed variable) so that bypassing the scan -- which would silence the warnings -- is still a killable breach. The corpus case caps (corpus_diagnostics.py) and the faithfulness oracles remain as they were; un-gating those is out of this ticket's scope (MF-033 and later). Acceptance proof (results/): the probe model now emits the exact "C1 touched by 10 actions" finding as a WARNING with a recommendation and exits 0 (probe/analyze-complexity-after.txt); this repository's own model, which previously failed "C1 touched by 14 actions", now emits the same warning and promotes cleanly (repo-model-analyze-complexity-after.txt). Delta vs MF-030 is zero: bound 699,840, distinct 231,621, depth 25 (tlc.txt). Retention oracles (kill_rate/effect_conformance/external_coverage) were not re-run because the model is byte-identical to MF-030; behavior retention is witnessed by the identical TLC run rather than by a fresh oracle pass, and no complexity decrease is claimed that would require them.

MF-028 measured that every adapter in this repository shells out, so the sandbox saw only the spawn and the verdict was `unobservable` forever. scripts/effect_conformance.py now carries WorkingTreeObserver: a working-tree snapshot diff (pure stdlib, no privileges, no dependency, runtime-agnostic) that snapshots roots before an execution window and diffs them after, turning a child's created/changed files into filesystem.write and vanished files into filesystem.delete. diff_effects grew an `out_of_process=` parameter carrying OutOfProcessObservation records -- POSITIVE evidence of which effect axes an observer covered -- and narrows a spawn's process-boundary finding to name only the axes still unwatched. MEASURED on this repo's own surface (results/observe_out_of_process.py drives the real, shelling-out ScaffoldProjectAdapter through its real subprocess.run against the real five declared ports): BEFORE = 2 observed effects, spec_tree DEAD, blanket boundary, verdict unobservable (the MF-028 state). AFTER = 17 observed effects, 15 child writes recovered out-of-process (all matching **/specs/**), spec_tree EXERCISED, a real GAP surfaced (ScaffoldProject's undeclared python spawn), and the boundary finding narrowed to "filesystem observed; network.connect, network.http, process.spawn unobserved". Verdict STILL unobservable -- honestly, because a filesystem diff cannot see a child's network, and that residual is named precisely (acceptance criterion branch 2). The four other ports read as honest dead_surface from a reduced single-action demo; declarations preserved, not deleted. MF-027 POLARITY SURVIVED, proven by tests (TestPolaritySurvivesOutOfProcessObservation): a spawn with no out-of-process evidence is still fully unobservable; filesystem-only coverage still leaves the network unobservable; only positive coverage of EVERY axis discharges a boundary (which a filesystem-only observer never reaches); a runtime refusal is untouched; and `out_of_process` is an evidence parameter, never a suppression flag (empty evidence downgrades nothing). report.ok still consults only the finding lists. Recommendation: RUN THE ORACLES ADVISORILY rather than chasing per-oracle verdict projection -- reaching a `clean` effect verdict on a shelling-out repo needs either network syscall capture (privileged, non-portable) or in-process invocation of every adapter (MF-028's "large" axis), and the payoff (a blocking gate) is what the 2026-07-20 advisory reframe already retired. entries.justification: AC-01 adds one variable (`architecture_scan`) and one action (`AnalyzeArchitecture`) to represent a command the CLI now genuinely has. An unrepresented command is not modeled behavior, and the same reasoning has licensed every previous scanner variable in this model (MF-011 complexity_gate, MF-014 corpus_gate, MF-013/MF-027 effect_conformance, MF-016 kill_test). The domain is 4-valued: unknown | coherent | divergent | unmappable. It is NOT collapsed to shrink the state space. `unmappable` is distinct from `unknown` for exactly the reason MF-027 grew `unobservable` on the effect oracle: "the scan has not run" and "the scan ran and could not see the target" are different facts, and merging them deletes the one verdict this epic exists to report. `divergent` is distinct from `coherent` because it is the finding, and the two select distinct CLI next-steps. Measured cost, recorded rather than argued down: static bound        699,840 -> 2,799,360   (x4, the domain size) TLC distinct        283,805 -> 1,292,951   (x4.6) TLC generated     6,209,780 -> 32,122,220  (x5.2) depth                    25 -> 26 wall clock              12s -> 58s The static bound now exceeds max_state_space_bound 1,000,000 and the distinct count exceeds max_distinct_states 500,000. Both are ADVISORY thresholds (MF-036) and both were left as they are: `max_distinct_states` was NOT raised to make the number look compliant, and the domain was NOT shrunk to fit under it. The owner measured these same figures independently before the ticket opened (specs/results/tlc-desired-epic-ac.txt) and recorded the 4.6x as accepted. No action in the model guards on `architecture_scan`, and no close, promotion, or case-generation path reads it. The variable is a record, not a gate.

refinement.detail: Two reductions were considered and both rejected on fidelity grounds. (1) Merge `unmappable` into `unknown` (domain 4 -> 3, bound 2,799,360 -> 2,099,520): rejected -- it deletes the MF-027 distinction between "not run" and "ran blind", which is the verdict AC-02's refusal semantics depend on. (2) Drop `architecture_scan` and let AnalyzeArchitecture touch only lastCommand/result (bound back to 699,840): rejected -- the command's whole output is the verdict, so a model that cannot see the verdict cannot represent the command. Beyond this ticket's delta no reduction to the existing model was found: the model's own architecture descriptor (results/architecture-self.txt) reports one component at Q = 0.000, so there is no cut available to take. That non-decomposition is itself this ticket's headline finding.

entries.narrative: AC-01 turned the structure `analyze complexity` computes internally into an addressable artifact: `tla-spec-dev analyze architecture`, with a text descriptor and a versioned JSON form (schema tla-spec-dev/architecture-descriptor v1) that AC-02 and AC-03 consume. The load-bearing finding is negative and is recorded as such. Run against the two real models available, the emergent clustering does NOT yield a usable architecture in either case: * specs/current/TlaSpecDevCli.tla -- ONE component, Q = 0.000. `lastCommand` and `result` are written by all 15 commands, so the variable interaction graph is effectively complete and greedy modularity finds nothing to separate. * examples/distributed_history/.../External.tla -- two components, Q = 0.047, but 9 of 12 actions cross the boundary and EVERY variable is written by some action that also writes into the other component. The reference example has no single-writer state at all. The descriptor reports that instead of presenting the one-component partition as an architecture. That refusal is the design decision this ticket most wanted to get right: with one component every variable is trivially "written inside its component", so a naive implementation reports zero single-writer violations and no ports -- a flawless architecture report for a model that has none, indistinguishable from the real thing. The ownership fields are `null` with a stated reason instead, and `partition.consumable_as_architecture` is published as the single field AC-02 must branch on to report `unmappable` rather than a false `coherent`. Because both real targets refuse, the descriptor would be vacuous without a second, non-inventive source of components. That source is a DECLARED partition (`architecture:` in spec_manifest.yaml, or --components), symmetric with AC-02's declared module map and justified by the same rule: a tool that picks its own boundary can define every finding out of existence. The tool measures the partition the project names and never writes one; an unreadable declaration is refused rather than silently replaced by the emergent clustering. Exercised against this repository's own model in results/architecture-self-declared-demo.txt, where a four-component declaration makes all 10 variables single-writer violations -- the measured cause of the non-decomposition, now expressed as ownership. CD-01 is honored: no proposed cut, no refactor, no target shape, no next step. The one judgment the tool makes -- "this partition is not a cut" -- ships with the criteria table that produced it (component_count >= 2, Q > 0, crossing fraction <= 0.5), so a reader can disagree with the rule rather than with a verdict handed down without one. The crossing-fraction rule reuses the R/W matrix's existing >half dense-row/dense-column convention rather than a threshold invented here, and Newman's Q >= 0.3 convention is reported beside the score but never applied as a criterion. Doctrine held throughout: exit 0 on any analyzable model however incoherent, nonzero only for the MF-030 unresolved-hierarchy fail-closed or an unreadable declaration; and `analyze architecture` on its own always reports `unmappable`, because it measures the model side and an unobserved target is never clean.

The defect was real and reproduced exactly as briefed: on the shipped three-module example the ledger measured Core.tla against External.cfg and recorded variables 0, actions 0, bound None, modularity 0.0 -- for a module with no variables and no actions. refinement.detail: Searched and found none that this ticket may take. AC-03 has no model delta to refine, so the search ran against the standing model, and it produced a result worth recording rather than a reduction. The obvious candidate is the one AC-01 named: specs/current has ONE emergent component at Q = 0.000, because lastCommand and result are written by all 15 commands. Splitting that god-pair would cut the interaction graph. It is not available here -- it is a production refactor of the CLI, outside AC-03's conflict keys (prompts/, templates/, references/case_modules.md, SKILL.md), and Move 3 requires explicit user approval besides. While rendering the brief this ticket measured something that sharpens the question for whoever does take it. The claim "this model does not decompose" is a claim about GREEDY modularity maximization, not about the model. Exhaustive enumeration of all 115,975 set partitions of the model's 10 variables, scored with the SHIPPED modularity function and the SHIPPED three criteria, finds TWO partitions that meet all three -- the best at Q = 0.0029 with a crossing-action fraction of 0.188 -- and the shipped CLI confirms it when the partition is handed back via --components ("the partition is a cut -- every criterion above is met"). Reproduction is checked in at results/ac03_df02_exhaustive_partition_search.py and the finding is filed as AC-03-DF-02. That is NOT a refinement to apply, and this ticket deliberately does not apply it. Q = 0.003 is negligible structure, and adopting the exhaustive search would have the tool NAME a cut the project never declared -- the exact CD-01 failure the refusal doctrine exists to prevent. What it changes is the wording of a claim the epic leans on, which is why it is a deferred finding for the owner and not a change here.

entries.narrative: AC-03 is the generation-time half of the epic: a descriptor is advice until it constrains the request. It ships prompts/implementation_brief.md (with templates/implementation_brief.md as the rendered shape) and prompts/aspect_decomposition.md, in the form prompts/coverage_audit.md established, plus the case-module/feature-module distinction stated once in SKILL.md under the Program Spec Rule. ZERO model delta, as the plan expected: ticket current == desired byte for byte, TLC green reproducing AC-01's figures exactly, and all three of specs/current, ticket current and ticket desired measuring 10 variables / 16 actions / 1 component / Q = 0.000. See results/model-delta.txt. THE DEMONSTRATION. Four briefs were rendered end-to-end by following the prompt, and they are kept as evidence because the interesting result is the spread, not any one of them: * OpenTicket, specs/current under a DECLARED 2-component partition (workflow | scanners) -- DEGRADED. Real constraints: writes only ticket_state/lastCommand/result, internal to workflow so it may not touch the scanner component at all, one declared effect port (spec_tree: filesystem.write **/specs/**), does not span so one commit point, and three of the variables it writes flagged as not single-writer. * AnalyzeComplexity, same descriptor, subject component named by the caller -- DEGRADED on two counts. Same partition, but the subject component owns nothing and has no internal action, so "this work belongs to scanners" restricts nothing by itself. The strongest clause in that brief is the measured SPAN: the action commits lastCommand/result in workflow and complexity_gate in scanners in one step, and the brief says the model asserts those land atomically -- honor it or report the model wrong. * OpenTicket, specs/current under the EMERGENT partition -- REFUSED, and the refusal artifact records verbatim what the vacuous brief would have said ("component C1, 10 of 10 variables, reaches nothing, zero violations"), so the failure mode is legible rather than theoretical. * CreateAccount, examples/distributed_history/.../Internal.tla, EMERGENT -- the only FULL brief, and it clears crossing_action_fraction by exactly zero. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE EPIC'S WORKING ASSUMPTIONS, both measured here. (1) AC-01's `consumable_as_architecture` is necessary but NOT sufficient for a non-vacuous brief. It is `partition_source == "declared" or decomposes`, which is right for AC-02 -- whose question is whether the project named a boundary to compare code against -- and wrong as AC-03's only gate, because it is true for ANY declared partition including a deliberately useless one. The prompt therefore layers three per-render vacuity tests on top of it: V1 (one component) refuses; V2 (the subject component owns nothing AND has no internal action) and V3 (crossing fraction > 0.5) degrade rather than refuse, because the write-set, effect-port and atomicity clauses are measured PER ACTION and survive a bad partition intact. The two DEGRADED renders above differ by exactly V2, from the same descriptor -- whether a brief constrains anything depends on which component the work lands in, not only on the partition score. (2) "Neither real model decomposes" is not what was measured. Internal.tla decomposes EMERGENTLY (2 components, Q = 0.0069, crossing fraction 0.50), and exhaustive search finds decomposing partitions of specs/current itself. See `refinement:` above and AC-03-DF-02. The refusal doctrine survives intact -- refusing to invent a cut is still right -- but the wording claims more than a greedy search establishes. A THIRD, SMALLER FINDING, filed as AC-03-DF-01 and defended against in the prompt: for a one-component partition the JSON reports ownership.single_writer_violations as null WITH a stated reason, but components[0].owns as the bare empty list []. A consumer reads that as "owns nothing" -- a plausible architectural fact -- when it means "undefined here". The text renderer says NOT MEASURABLE; the machine-readable contract that AC-02 and AC-03 actually read does not. Gate A refuses before the field can be reached, which is why the guard is a gate and not a caveat. DOCTRINE. CD-01 holds: neither prompt proposes a cut, a refactor, a target shape or a next step. Move 3's shapes are the vocabulary the measured facts are STATED in -- the brief says "these are your declared ports", not "push effects to the edges"; "the model says these commit together", not "introduce a commit point". Both are advisory and gate nothing. The Program Spec Rule is not weakened: the aspect prompt forbids a case module from declaring any state, constant or action, requires EXTENDS over INSTANCE/LOCAL, and keeps the removal test (delete every case module and the program is still fully represented) as the rule rather than a note. WHAT IS NOT SHOWN, and both prompts say so in their own validation sections: nothing here measures whether a brief changes what a coding agent produces. The prompts make the ask derivable and checkable field by field. Whether a derivable ask yields more coherent code is an empirical question this ticket did not answer and could not -- it belongs to the epic's evaluation tickets. Until then a brief is a hypothesis with good provenance, not a result.

refinement.detail: Three reductions were considered against the landed design and all three were rejected on fidelity grounds -- each would have made a report LOOK cleaner while measuring less. (1) Treat an intra-component code edge as a convergence, collapsing the report to two categories instead of four. Rejected: with a one-component map every edge is then a convergence and the tool reports a perfect score for a codebase it never constrained. Internal edges are counted and explicitly NOT checked against a port. (2) Downgrade the extraction blind spots (dynamic imports, unparsed files, non-Python files, unmapped modules) from `unmappable` to a warning attached to a `coherent` verdict -- the smaller state space and the friendlier report. Rejected; this is MF-027 verbatim: a clean report on a target you could not see is indistinguishable from a clean report on one you could. The dogfood shows the cost of the decision honestly -- this repository's own scripts/ tree has zero divergences under a falsifiable partition and STILL reports unmappable, for three computed-name imports, one shell script, and one sibling package. (3) Drop the `unfalsifiable_coherence` check, on the argument that a fully ported architecture with no divergences is simply coherent. Rejected after measuring it: under the three-component partition this ticket first wrote, this repository's model ports every pair, so no code edge could have diverged and `coherent` would have been true by construction. That is the same false clean as (2), arriving through the model instead of the extractor. No reduction to the TLA+ model was found beyond AC-01's, and for AC-01's reason: the model's own architecture descriptor reports one component at Q = 0.000, so there is no cut available to take. AC-02 measured that from a second direction -- see the dogfood finding.

entries.narrative: AC-02 implements the reflexion model (Murphy, Notkin & Sullivan) on top of AC-01's descriptor: a DECLARED map from production modules to model components, an extracted Python dependency graph, and a diff reported as convergences, divergences (with file:line at the SITE of the dependency), and absences. Internal edges are counted as a fourth category and deliberately not checked -- they crossed no boundary. Shipped as scripts/architecture_reflexion.py, wired into `analyze architecture --code <tree> --map <map.yaml>`, with its own JSON schema (tla-spec-dev/architecture-reflexion v1) and a standalone CLI. Half a check is a usage error: --code without --map would make the TOOL pick the boundary, and --map without --code reports every port absent. THE DELIVERABLE IS THE DOGFOOD, and it took three runs to state honestly. Full write-up in results/dogfood-findings.txt; the short form: 1. The acceptance command as the plan wrote it -- no declared partition -- reports `unmappable` and does not run the diff at all. The model has one component (Q = 0.000; lastCommand and result are written by all fifteen commands). Had the diff run, all 258 code edges would have been internal to that single component: 0 divergences, 0 absences, `coherent`. The report prints "NOT RUN" instead of three zeroes, because zero findings from a comparison that never happened is the false clean in its purest form. This is the branch AC-01 published partition.consumable_as_architecture for, used exactly as intended. 2. With a DECLARED four-component partition (surface / tickets / corpus / kill, cut by the state each command commits) the check runs and is FALSIFIABLE: corpus<->kill and kill<->tickets have no port, because no action of the model touches kill_test together with ticket_state or with a corpus verdict. 34 modules all mapped, 4 components all realized, 258 edges, 140 internal, 118 convergences, 0 divergences, 0 absences. The two kill-test scripts reach only budgets.py, which is in surface and ported. That is a genuine falsifiable negative result about this codebase. The verdict is still `unmappable`, now for five extraction blind spots: three computed-name importlib.import_module calls, scripts/run_tlc.sh (no extractor), and spec_double_compiler/ (first-party, beside the code root, outside --code). 3. The COARSER three-component partition this ticket wrote first -- folding kill_test in with the other scanner verdicts, an entirely natural reading -- ports every pair, so no code edge could diverge and `coherent` would have been true by construction. `unfalsifiable_coherence` fires and refuses it. Runs 2 and 3 are both defensible readings of the same model, separated by one variable's placement. That is the ticket's central caution and it is stated in the reference rather than buried: the map and the partition are where the lying would happen, the tool measures the declaration it is handed, and it cannot audit that declaration. What it CAN do it does -- the map must place every module in the tree (leaving one out is `unmapped_module`, never cleaner), every declared component must be realized, no module may be in two components, and every placement is published. `unfalsifiable_coherence` catches only the fully degenerate case; a merely COARSE partition still reports a real-looking clean, and that limitation is documented. MF-027 is enforced structurally, not by convention. The verdict property reads nothing but the report: no environment variable, no flag, no manifest key. Suppression-shaped keys in the map (assume_coherent, allow_unmapped, waived, justification, accepted_divergences, ignore, exclude, skip, trusted, override, ...) are SCANNED, reported under ignored_suppression_keys, and never honored -- the shape scripts/effect_conformance.py uses, because a silently ignored key is nearly as bad as an honored one. TestNothingDowngradesAnUnobservableVerdict holds it shut from four directions: sixteen map keys, four environment variables, four plausible CLI flags (argparse rejects them), and a source-level assertion that the verdict property mentions no configuration at all. Evidence: results/suppression-ignored.txt, the same tree run twice with identical findings. A positive case exists, which matters because without one "always unmappable" would have passed every refusal test in the suite. The fixture is a three-component pipeline model whose ports permit ingest<->transform and transform<->deliver but not ingest<->deliver, with matching code: results/fixture-coherent.txt reports `coherent` with the unported pair named, so the clean result is falsifiable. results/fixture-divergent.txt adds one import and reports both the import and the call site with file:line; results/fixture-absence.txt removes an edge and reports the dead port. Advisory throughout. Exit 0 on `divergent` AND on `unmappable`; nonzero (2) only for an unusable map or an unreadable code tree -- "I could not measure this". No close, promotion, or case-generation path reads architecture_scan. CD-01 holds: the report names edges, ports, and files, and never says where a module should live; a test asserts the rendered text carries no move-suggesting phrasing. Coverage limits are stated in the report itself rather than left to be discovered: Python only; static resolution only; in-tree edges only, so a component that reaches a database or a socket directly is invisible (that axis belongs to scripts/effect_conformance.py). One limit was FOUND by the dogfood and fixed: imports resolving to a first-party package beside the code root were being filed as third-party, which meant narrowing --code would delete real edges from the graph with nothing recorded. They are now a named blind spot.

entries.narrative: EV-02 ran the evals as a fact-finding mission and wrote the follow-up charter. Six run records under examples/validation/runs/ (ex4 x3, ex5 x2, ex6 x1), each scored against predictions committed before any dispatch. Aim 1: control green on both arms, then 4 of 6 for the corpus alone and 6 of 6 with the content-asserting provider, per fault class, per arm, against MF-038's 0 of 9 -- with the parameter-recovery bound stated so the comparison is not overclaimed. Aim 2: EV-01's ratios reproduce exactly, and a blind agent's Given-form aspect turned 60 authored lines into 38 cases that killed exactly what the 330-case whole-view corpus killed. Aim 3: generation byte-identical again, execution byte-identical across 14 executions including twelve failing ones, and seeded failures replaying exactly -- the half EV-01 could not do. The architecture half scored precision 1.000 and recall 1.000 against the owner's enumerated answer key, with zero false positives on the coherent twin, and every refusal held on both real models. The centrepiece experiment passed: a blind agent handed a divergent codebase and an editable map fixed the code and left all four declarations byte-identical. Against that, the unflattering half, which is the half worth having: `coherent` is obtainable on that same divergent codebase for about six lines of YAML, 12 of 203 partitions do it, every one of them fails the model's own decomposition criteria, none records a blind spot, and the mitigation for it already exists -- in a prompt rather than in the program. The check measures import topology and not interaction, anything outside --code is free, a generated corpus cannot see guard relaxation by construction, and ordering is invisible at every oracle layer. Five findings filed, none fixed. And the single most valuable result came from neither lever: authoring an aspect from the public surface revealed that the public surface is FALSE of the model -- a failed item can never reach the ledger, though the README promises it -- which no corpus could ever catch, because a case module may not add an action and there is no action to enter. NEXT-EPIC.md carries all of it forward, including what not to re-litigate.

entries.narrative: RP-04 fixed CM-01-DF-03 and CM-01-DF-02 and changed no TLA+. DF-03 was the epic's recurring defect wearing its clearest costume: on the shipped example the descriptor TEXT named all nine variables it could not size, and the ledger JSON recorded "used 4, percent 0.0, within_cap true" against a 1,000,000 cap for a model TLC measures at 49,386 distinct states. Bound COMPLETENESS is now a published fact -- BoundCompleteness on the descriptor, five keys in the JSON payload the CD-03 fitness rules read, three metrics keys plus a caveat in the ledger, and a line under the number in both renderers. The cap comparison is made only in the direction it is sound: over the cap survives incompleteness, at-or-under does not and is recorded as null with the reason. An incomplete bound is an advisory finding (state_space_bound_partial), never a block; the CLI still exits 0. RE-MEASUREMENT, and the part worth reading twice: CM-01-DF-03's own blast_radius claimed "the repository's own model resolves every variable". It does not, and never has -- lastCommand and result have had no resolvable domain since MF-020, and tests/test_analyze_complexity.py has asserted exactly that across the nine-ticket calibration chain. So every bound this repository has recorded, 2,799,360 included, is a product over an 8-variable subset. The consequence is small only because this model is OVER its cap, which is the one comparison that survives: bound, variables, actions, modularity and within_cap are all unchanged, and 279.9% is now published as percent_lower_bound with percent null. That is recorded, not smoothed, and the false claim in the deferred-findings entry is corrected in place. The calibration chain was extended in its established style with the completeness facts, since a chain of multiplications over a subset is only meaningful while the subset holds still. DF-02 was a five-line parser fix: a bare TLC keyword line closes an INVARIANT block, tested against a keyword set case-SENSITIVELY so an invariant named `Alias` is not swallowed; the same set now closes a CONSTANTS block, replacing an ad-hoc prefix tuple. The CFG_KEYWORDS workaround is left in scripts/spec_evolution.py -- it is CM-01's file, not RP-04's and not RP-03's -- with both experiments recorded showing it is now dead code. Two more instances of the same honest-prose / misleading-artifact pattern were found inside the two files RP-04 owns and fixed in the same pass: the ledger recorded a TLC distinct-state count with no flag for a run that did not finish (while analyze() is careful to check max_distinct_states only when report.complete), and it recorded an action count with no flag when the count came from the FALLBACK primes heuristic (while the descriptor says so in prose). One limit was chosen and filed rather than crossed: a non-comparable bound delta still feeds the ledger's DIRECTION, which is a real gate, and RP-04 records `comparable: false` with a printed NOT LIKE-FOR-LIKE note instead of changing what refuses a close (RP-04-DF-01). One process note, recorded because this ticket is about flattering numbers: the first close of RP-04 read results/tlc-current.txt, which at that moment held the MCsmall.cfg run, and computed a 98.4% distinct-state DECREASE against EV-02's full-config figures -- a comparison between two different configs wearing the costume of a reduction. It was caught before the entry was committed, the entry was discarded rather than annotated, the full-config run was put at the conventional path, and the ticket was re-closed. The corrected entry reports direction=zero. This is also a small finding about the convention: `close ticket` takes the first of results/tlc-current.txt, tlc.txt, tlc-baseline.txt with no check that the report it found was produced from the cfg the ledger measures.

refinement.detail: Searched, found none applicable: RP-02's model delta is zero, so there is no representation to refine. The search WAS run against the one place this ticket could have reached for the model, and it was refused on the record MF-029 already wrote. The obvious way to make an existentially quantified argument recoverable is to have the model STATE it -- a `lastInternalAction` marker, exactly the mechanism `params_from_action_marker` already reads. Rejected twice over: the state pair already implies the element for every `v' = v \cup {i}` / `v' = v \ {i}` conjunct, so the marker would add representation to carry information the corpus already holds; and max_state_space_bound is at 279.9% of cap on this model, where MF-019 measured that a single boolean variable breaches it. Recovery therefore stays generator-side, which is also what keeps it cheaply revertible -- reverting is deleting a mechanism from one module, and nothing in the spec moves. Two representation choices inside the mechanism were made the cheaper way and are recorded here rather than left implicit. (1) The recipe keeps EVERY matching set conjunct as a cross-checking witness instead of picking one, which costs a tuple per parameter and buys a real refusal: `Deliver(i)` is witnessed by both `queue` and `delivered`, and witnesses that disagree yield UNCHECKED rather than a silent winner. (2) `consumed_observations` was added as a SEPARATE property rather than folded into `unavailable_checks`, because the two claims are different strengths -- set-membership spends "which element moved in v", it does not make the whole after-value of v tautological the way `written-through` does, and collapsing them would have overstated the price of the recovery.

refinement.detail: RP-07 carries zero TLA+ model delta (results/zero-model-delta.txt; the ledger header records direction=zero vs RP-05) and its whole diff is two files under test_graph/. No variable, action or domain was added or removed, so no reduction search over the representation applies. The refinement search that does apply is over the FIX, and four alternatives were considered against the reproduction in results/diagnosis.md: (1) Relax or delete the executor's descendant contract. REJECTED, and it is also not reachable: test_graph/build-logic and test_graph/sdk are symlinks into $SKILL_MANAGER_HOME, so editing them would edit the installed skill for every repository. The contract was also correct -- the surviving process was real, and the executor's reap of it reaches a daemon shared with the outer build. (2) Drain-and-tolerate: have the node wait for the daemon and pass anyway, or exempt "known daemon" command lines. REJECTED as making a check pass by weakening what it asserts. A 7200-second idle daemon does not exit inside any bounded wait, so this is exemption dressed as patience. (3) Stop recopying the probe project each run (retain build/), so the nested build never compiles Kotlin and never forks the daemon. REJECTED: the warm-project arm of the A/B does show 0 live descendants, but it wins by not exercising the from-scratch path the probe exists to exercise, and it makes the node's result depend on leftover state from a previous run. (4) Pin kotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=in-process. CHOSEN. It removes the fork rather than tolerating it, keeps the nested compile inside the tree the node owns and can reap, changes no assertion, and is confined to the node's own subprocess invocation. Measured against arms (2)/(3) in the three-arm table in results/diagnosis.md. The added assertion `nested probe build left no live descendants` is additive representation in the NODE, not in the model, and it is deliberately narrower than the executor's check (bounded drain, node-body subtree only). It exists so a regression names the offending command lines instead of bare PIDs. The executor's check remains the authority; the node cannot make a violating run green.

entries.narrative: Full diagnosis with the reproduction: specs/tickets/RP-07/results/diagnosis.md. RP-07 diagnoses the one red node EV-02 escalated rather than filed. The verdict is the first of the three offered outcomes: a REAL defect, in the probe, fixed. Not flakiness, not a wrong assertion, not an unsatisfiable environment assumption. Reproduced twice on this worktree with the probe unmodified: `specWorkflow` fails at `spec.workflow.failure_cleanup_probe` with "node launcher exited with live descendants", different PIDs each run -- matching EV-02's report exactly. A 0.4s `ps` sampler run alongside the second reproduction resolves the reported PID and its full ancestry (results/descendant-ancestry.txt): outer Gradle daemon -> SDK perl process-group supervisor -> `uv run` node launcher -> node python -> nested gradlew -> nested single-use Gradle daemon -> `org.jetbrains.kotlin.daemon.KotlinCompileDaemon --daemon-autoshutdownIdleSeconds=7200`. The survivor is the Kotlin compile daemon: a shared, user-scoped service with a two-hour idle lifetime, i.e. one designed to outlive the build that started it. It is forked on every single run because `copy_probe_project` recopies the project with `ignore_patterns("build", ...)`, so the nested build always compiles the `build-logic` Kotlin plugin from scratch, and the Kotlin Gradle plugin's default execution strategy is `daemon`. A three-arm A/B on an isolated copy, all Kotlin daemons killed before each arm, with a harness that builds the same descendant inventory the executor builds (results/descendant-contract-harness.py): warm project, no Kotlin compile -> 0 live after exit; fresh copy, as shipped -> 1 live, the KotlinCompileDaemon; fresh copy plus in-process strategy -> 0 live. The warm-project arm is the control that isolates the cause. The contract was right to fail this. The executor does not merely report the survivor, it TERMs then KILLs it -- and that daemon is keyed on ~/Library/Application Support/kotlin/daemon and shared with the outer build, so the reap reaches outside the node. A node that forks a machine-scoped service into its own process tree is doing something the contract should refuse. Why it was green before, on this same machine: MF-027's green run of this node is 2026-07-19, and at that commit `awaitWithTimeout` was a plain `process.waitFor(timeout)` with no descendant inventory at all. Commit 0e3f00c (2026-07-23, "chore: upgrade test graph observability scaffold") replaced test_graph/build-logic and test_graph/sdk with symlinks into $SKILL_MANAGER_HOME and brought in the POSIX process-group supervisor and the descendant contract. The probe's behavior did not change on 2026-07-23; the instrument that can see it arrived. The leak was newly DETECTED, not newly introduced -- which is the scaffold upgrade working as intended. Fix: pin kotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=in-process on both channels -- `-P` on the command line, because command-line project properties propagate into the `build-logic` included build where the compilation actually happens, and `-D` in GRADLE_OPTS alongside the pre-existing `-Dorg.gradle.daemon=false`. Confirmed the compile still happens (the run populates build-logic/build/classes/kotlin/main/) rather than being skipped. test_graph/README.md gains a section naming the requirement so a future edit does not quietly drop the flags. Evidence integrity: nothing was weakened. The seven pre-existing probe assertions are unchanged and all still pass; one was added. The added in-node check is strictly narrower than the executor's (it drains up to 20s where the executor allows none, and inspects only the node body's subtree), and it is a diagnostic that writes offending command lines to node-logs/spec.workflow.failure_cleanup_probe.lingering-descendants.log -- not a replacement gate. The executor's ProcessContractViolation check is untouched and still fails the node if the in-node check is ever wrong. Nothing under $SKILL_MANAGER_HOME was edited. Result: specWorkflow PASSED on three consecutive runs (results/ test-graphs.txt), repository unit tests 944 passed / 0 failed (940 on the epic tip; the +4 are parametrized YAML-parse cases over this ticket's own scaffolded files), spec-unit validation passed, zero TLA+ model delta. One thing this ticket did NOT establish: whether any other repository using this scaffold has nodes that spawn nested Gradle builds and would hit the same contract. The `in-process` requirement is a general consequence of the contract meeting the Kotlin plugin's default, not something specific to this probe, and it currently lives only in this repository's test_graph/README.md. Recorded in specs/desired_program_model/deferred_findings.yaml.

entries.narrative:
EV-03 re-ran the whole eval suite against the repaired tree (RP-01..RP-05, RP-07 merged) and re-scored it against the SAME committed predictions in examples/validation/PREDICTIONS.md, which was not edited. The headline artifact is examples/validation/runs/ROUND-2-DELTA.md; the per-arm records are runs/ex4-run4..6, runs/ex5-run3..4 and runs/ex6-run2.
MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED -- what worked. RP-01: the 203-partition sweep of the divergent fixture reports 0 `coherent`, down from 12, with all 203 exiting 0. The number that had to be checked separately is that it removed no TRUE findings: zero of round 1's 71 divergence verdicts were lost, and 20 previously-suppressed ones were released (71 -> 91). RP-01's basis_limits vs blind_spots distinction was verified independently -- 67 of round 1's 71 divergence verdicts carry partition_does_not_decompose, so filing that as a blind spot would have suppressed 67 real findings to remove the same 12 false cleans. DP-2 re-scored MISSED -> CAUGHT, DP-2b CONFIRMED -> CLOSED on the measured path. RP-03: case modules generate from the documented location (round 1: exit 150), their corpora carry 50/50 and 6/6 recovered arguments (round 1: 0/50 and 0/6), and a Given's corpus EXECUTES against the project's unchanged adapters -- a capability that did not exist in round 1.

entries.narrative: TWO HALVES, and the second matters more. (1) `score_tools.py scaffold` emits one skeleton per arm per judge with the anchors and the seven scoring rules INLINE -- READ OUT OF references/eval_scorecard.md rather than transcribed, so there is one source of truth and a judge reads the bar for a score in the same file where the score is written. The skeleton records the rubric's digest and `check` refuses to let a judge fill in a card scaffolded against a rubric that has since changed. Blinding is the DEFAULT: labels are drawn from a pool that excludes every label any prior round published, and the mapping goes to UNBLINDING.md outside every card directory; --unblinded requires --reason and writes it into the key. Scaffolding twice REFUSES and writes NOTHING -- not one file, including the ones that would not have collided. (2) `history --example E` prints one example's rows with the instrument changes marked BETWEEN them, and `audit` EXECUTES the four reading rules the ticket asked to be written down. That is deliberate: a declaration nothing executes will drift, which is the exact class of artifact this epic keeps finding stale, so `audit` fails if references/eval_scorecard.md declares an R-H rule with no check behind it. WHAT THE HISTORY VIEW FOUND, beyond the three worked examples it was given. Two live stale rows, both filed and neither fixed. PA-05-DF-01: the epic document's own baseline table has the D5 attribution INVERTED -- the best-ever 4 went to the TREATMENT under the rerun, not the control -- in the document every ticket agent in this epic is told to read first. PA-05-DF-02: every EVAL-RERUN number this epic uses as a live baseline was measured before TWO later instrument changes and none has been re-affirmed, including GOAL-cases-drive-ports' 56-of-56, where EVAL-SUPPRESS flipped exactly one cell and flipped it on ONE ARM ONLY. Evidence: specs/results/scorecards/HISTORY-ab_quota_ledger.md, specs/results/scorecards/INSTRUMENT-LOG.toml, and tests/test_score_tools.py (34 cases, all 34 failing on the parent tree 1cad5ea, verified by archiving it and running this file against it).

A port's REGION could have been declared in the manifest as a `writes:` key beside the port, which is simpler to implement and would let a port name a region the model does not support. It was refused under declaration_executability_rule: it is a second declaration of a fact the model already carries, and its failure mode is that the declared region and the action write sets drift with nothing able to notice. Deriving the region from written_variables -- the same function the negative corpus uses to choose what it may negate -- means the declaration cannot be WRONG about the model, only DISAGREE with it, and the disagreement is counted and printed every run in both directions. The one measurable complexity cost is corpus size, and it went DOWN on every corpus it was run beside: 43,128 -> 1,855 on the A/B fixture (23x), 99,817 -> 29,921 on this repository's own model with 15 declared ports. The flag is off by default, so no existing corpus moves at all.

Those numbers are about the FIXTURE, never about this repository's own model, and `kill_rate` here means the latter. Reporting them in this field would quote a number against the wrong instrument, which is the hazard PA-04-DF-02 filed.

(1) PA-03-DF-03 / PA-04-DF-01 -- seed a blatant fault inside the declared port's region so a port-scoped instrument can have a green positive control. DECLINED for the third time, by the ticket both findings assign it to. PA-01 schedule_revision 2 permits repairing an instrument BEFORE a measurement and forbids it after an unflattering signal; PA-06 IS the measurement, so no legitimate ordering exists. Carried forward with its protocol spelled out -- seal the prediction, seed the control, run it, in that order, in a ticket that is not deciding a goal. entries.narrative: specs/results/scorecards/ports-as-adapters/RESULTS.md is the ledger, with PREDICTIONS-SCORED.md, UNBLINDING.md, DETERMINISM.md, channels/ADVERSARIAL.md and six sealed cards beside it. In short: ARM C SETTLES THE PREDECESSOR'S CONFOUND, FOR THE PROMPT. A control prompt longer than the hexagonal one and asking for nothing architectural scored D3 = 1 from both blind judges against arm B's 4 and arm A's 2, and its author, asked what it REJECTED, named the exact seam arm B built and declined it on merit. Length does not produce structure here. AND THAT IS THE ONLY GOOD NEWS. GOAL-port-reach is a SPLIT -- clause 1 met on PA-M12, clause 2 not met with twelve red control/instrument pairs. GOAL-cases-drive-ports is MISSED: 64 of 64 strictly comparable cells identical on every pairing of three arms, 88 of 88 over all rows for A vs C, and the one diverging cell in the whole three-arm port-binding table is a fault the hexagonal arm LOST. GOAL-complexity-measurable is MET and is not a claim that anything got simpler -- the produced-code figures support no simplification claim for any arm, and the smallest artifact on every size figure is the control that got no architectural guidance at all. THE FRESH ADVERSARIAL CHANNEL CORRECTED THIS TICKET'S OWN NUMBERS TWICE and found the round's most important result -- THE NULL WAS ENTAILED. An exhaustive 28,561-sequence observational fingerprint measures the three arms' MUTATED trees identical on 10 of 11 rows, so "the arms do not diverge" is a consequence of the re-anchoring succeeding and this experiment can only diverge where it FAILS. It also measured the repaired positive control unobservable in one step on three of four trees, and the probe that certifies it unable to fail -- a no-op mutant reports HOLDS. P07's own sealed row named that in advance as this epic's worst possible own goal. FINDINGS BY CHANNEL 1 : 12 : 4 : 2. Eighteen of nineteen came from asking an agent what it REJECTED or telling it to attack. The suite produced its first finding in four rounds and it fired at this ticket's own helper. Five of fifteen predictions FAILED, three of them negatives; one is SUPERSEDED. ELEVEN FINDINGS FILED, NOTHING FIXED. The deferment budget of 5 is deliberately exceeded and every row is `escalated` rather than carried, because PA-06 is the last ticket and there is no sibling to carry to. The alternative was to not report findings during the ticket whose entire purpose is to report them. ACCEPTANCE. `uv run --with pytest --with pyyaml python -m pytest tests -q` -> 1 failed, 1177 passed; the single failure is PA-06-DF-05 and it is left red on purpose. `score_tools.py check` -> 6 cards, 0 problems. `index` -> exit 0. `audit` -> 0 violations, after PA-06's own change turned three PA-04 claims SUPERSEDED-UNMARKED and six of its own cards OPEN, resolved by superseding the claims forward and recording a note beside each card. A reading rule that fires on its own author's cards is a reading rule doing its job.

No representation refinement follows: the model was not touched and no boundary changed. entries.narrative: FI-02, the epic's thesis ticket. references/architecture_advice.md S2 applied to this repository's own instruments for the first time. ENUMERATED 37 rows, of which 5 are classified NOT an instrument after being checked rather than assumed (fitness_functions, budgets, skill_feedback, case_modules coverage, score_tools index -- each refuses nothing, by its own docstring). Of the 32 instruments, 23 now ship a re-runnable demonstrated FAILING input and 27 a demonstrated PASSING input. NINE CANNOT BE SHOWN TO FAIL and each says why, in the registry, in its own row. Nine rows additionally carry a DEMONSTRATED BLIND SPOT: a genuine break the instrument does not report. That column is the more interesting half. The blinding sanitiser goes red on a leak with no substitution rule and stays CLEAN on the exact sentence PA-06-DF-11 measured. run_controls.py cannot measure a ported tree at all. run_port_swap.py prints a red control and exits 0. The TLA+ descriptor sits 432x over its own declared bound and exits 0, by design. And the tripwire this ticket repaired still cannot see a consumer that reads its JSON without naming it -- which is the route the one real reader takes. THE TRIPWIRE. PA-06-DF-05 is fixed and NOT by renaming the searched string. What was a substring grep is now an AST reference scan (an import under any alias, or a string whose WHOLE value is a path or module token) plus a taint analysis onto conditions, and it drops specs/**, which the plan declares out of model. It gained a second test that IS the invariant the docstring always stated -- nothing gates on the output -- which does reach specs/. Its cost is named: two exempt files, both of them files whose subject is the scanner, pinned by a test that asserts they would otherwise be flagged. NO NEW GATE. Nothing here refuses anything about the repository's design. The runner exits non-zero for one reason only: a DECLARED demonstration stopped reproducing, which means the instrument changed or the demonstration went stale, and both are things a reader has to be told. refinement.detail: SEARCHED, FOUND NONE, AND THE REASON IS THE MEASUREMENT RULE. FI-06 is the epic's evaluation ticket: its whole product is a report, and its standing instruction is FILE FINDINGS, FIX NOTHING. Every refinement this ticket could have proposed is a change to an instrument it is measuring with, so applying one would move a number during the report that number is in. Twelve candidates were found and every one was FILED rather than refined: FI-06-DF-01 (eight instruments absent from the registry -- registering run_arm_swap.py is four lines and would have turned 26-of-35 into 27-of-36, which is the number-fitting the rule exists to forbid), FI-06-DF-02 (the twelve pytest slots with no expect_output), FI-06-DF-03 (two slots with no seeded break), and nine more. Each carries a suggested_fix for whoever owns the next round.

entries.narrative: specs/results/scorecards/falsifiable-instruments/RESULTS.md is the narrative ledger, with channels/ADVERSARIAL.md and three per-goal RESULT files beside it. WHAT THE MACHINE-CHECKED CORE ABOVE CANNOT EXPRESS. The close reports `direction=zero (vs FI-05)` and `max_state_space_bound OVER CAP at 111.1%`. Both are inherited: FI-06 changed no model, no adapter and no production file, and the bound was already over the cap at FI-05. The bound is also a LOWER bound -- the product over 7 of 9 declared variables, with `lastCommand` and `result` unresolved -- and this ticket did not resolve them, because doing so would be a change made during a measurement. THE FIGURE THIS TICKET DID RECORD, AND IT IS NOT THIS ONE. FI-06's produced-code descriptor figures over the three judged arms sit in the mechanical block of RESULTS.md section 2 and are NEVER SCORED (thermometer_rule; MF-020: a metric falling is not evidence a design improved). They disagree with D2, which by the card's own scoring rule 7 is a finding and is filed as FI-06-DF-05: the arms separate by an order of magnitude on branch_points_in_effectful_modules (10 / 1 / 10) and on declared_interfaces (0 / 1 / 0), while D2 scores all three identically at 2 -- as it has on 27 of 27 cards ever written about this example. THE THREE GOALS. GOAL-instruments-can-fail MISSED on its only target ("nothing is silently omitted"); GOAL-scorecard-carries-a-delta MISSED on D4 and D5; GOAL-fixture-can-diverge MET, narrowly. Baseline, measured, target and verdict with a reason for each are in RESULTS.md and in the per-goal files. FINDINGS BY CHANNEL, 0 : 16 : 1 : 1 : 12 over the whole epic -- thirty findings, ZERO from the suite, which was green throughout while three instruments were missing from the enumeration and one shipped validator was red on the repository's own model. NOTHING WAS FIXED.

entries.narrative: Path: specs/results/scorecards/subtract-to-measure/SM-01-RESULTS.md, and the before-state it is read against at specs/results/scorecards/subtract-to-measure/before-state/README.md. WHAT THIS CLOSE IS. SM-01 removed nothing and repaired nothing. It seeded 9 gap mutants and 2 positive controls in the gaps SM-02 and SM-03 are about to open, measured them against 7 detectors, captured the toolchain's produced-code descriptor over four trees, and sealed 12 predictions with 6 negatives BEFORE the runner was ever pointed at a real mutant. The git history carries that ordering: seeds at 68a826f, predictions at b2b8e9c, numbers at cecf3b6. THE MEASURED ALTERNATIVE THAT WAS REJECTED, and it is the one worth recording. The obvious way to price the [ports.*] machinery was to mutate the machinery itself -- apply_wiring's swap line, adapter_for_case's port-first sort key, the label resolution in load_mappings. Each of those has a pytest node that goes red today, so each would have produced a flattering table. All three were rejected as NOT GAP MUTANTS: after SM-02 the mutated code does not exist, so the after half cannot be run and the row decides nothing. What is seeded instead is a fault in the SUBJECT -- the far side of the declared port, and the manifest that outlives the binding -- which is re-runnable on a tree the machinery has been cut out of. Same reasoning retired the `fake =` key mutant to [[not_seedable]]. THE FINDING THE CORE CANNOT EXPRESS. SM-GM-P3 survives all six columns the port-swap machinery owns, at 1543 executed cases each, while the positive control dies on those same six in the same run. The swap cannot detect that its own fake is not a fake -- the one failure a swap exists to make impossible. Filed as SM-01-DF-04, not fixed, because SM-01 is a measurement and because the repair is not obvious: asserting that two wirings DISAGREE would be wrong, since a fake is supposed to be a working implementation of the same interface. AND THE ONE ABOUT THIS TICKET'S OWN INSTRUMENT. The first run scored SM-GM-I2 and SM-GM-I3 as kills on the strength of a single failing node that was this runner's OWN catalogue-integrity test reacting to this runner's own mutation. Found by reading raw new_failing_nodes rather than verdicts; excluded from the verdict, reported per cell as self_detected_nodes, and covered by two tests including one that the exclusion cannot grow. A shipped tripwire also caught the ticket -- test_no_reader_of_this_instrument_gates_ on_its_output went red on the new test file -- and it was fixed by not naming the module rather than by lengthening the tripwire's exemption list. PREDICTIONS: 3 PASS, 4 FAIL of the 7 decidable at this ticket. P03 failed because my own mutant was under-powered, which is recorded as a defect in the mutant rather than reinterpreted into a finding about the registry. N01-N05 are SM-05's. Acceptance: 1370 passed in 361.85s. Findings SM-01-DF-01..05 filed, none fixed, budget 5 spent exactly.

entries.narrative: Path: specs/results/scorecards/subtract-to-measure/SM-03-RESULTS.md, read against specs/results/scorecards/subtract-to-measure/after-state/instrument-sweep-after.md and its before-state counterpart. NOTHING WAS DELETED, AND THE TICKET'S STATED DEFAULT WAS DELETION. FI-06 said twelve pytest failing slots assert only `expect_exit = 0`, "which pytest returns for a passing run and a fully skipped one". SM-01 seeded both skip shapes and measured the sentence: a module-level skip collects nothing, pytest exits 5, and those slots ALREADY went red. Only a pytestmark skip -- collected then skipped, exit 0 -- reported `ok`. So the hole is a demonstration that goes VACUOUS, not one that DISAPPEARS, and the twelve are UNCOUNTED rather than hollow. A hollow instrument should be deleted; an uncounted one should be counted. All twelve repaired, zero deleted. THE MEASURED ALTERNATIVE THAT WAS REJECTED, and it is the one that would have flattered the number. `ticket-state-agreement` is classified `no-instrument-exists`, watches nothing, and SM-01 recorded that "the removal's cost is already paid in full". Deleting that one row would have moved the ratio from 33/47 to 33/46 by arithmetic alone, with no instrument gained and none lost. That is `denominator_rule`'s exact prohibition -- a ratio that rises because the denominator shrank -- and taking it while reporting a falling ratio elsewhere would have been laundering one number through another. The row stays and stays counted. THE COUNT MOVED THE OTHER WAY. 26 of 35 -> 33 of 47; the ratio FELL from 74.3% to 70.2%. Numerator +7 = 5 new rows carrying a demonstration + 2 repairs of rows whose "no-demonstration-constructible" SM-GM-I4 showed was a fact about demonstrate.py shelling pytest at REPO_ROOT rather than about the instrument. Denominator +12, from the eighteen executables the enumeration could not see. FI-06 said "at least eight"; a derived check found eighteen on its first run, including demonstrate.py itself and run_gap_mutants.py, which SM-01 shipped unregistered in this same epic. THE LARGEST PART OF THE WORK MOVES NO FIGURE. Repairing a slot that reported `ok` for the wrong reason so that it reports `ok` for the right one reads identically in the count. The only evidence it changed is SM-GM-I1, which survived the registry at SM-01 and dies against it now: "0 test(s) passed, declared exactly 4" and "4 test(s) SKIPPED, declared 0". THE REGISTRY BLIND SPOT, fixed without lengthening a list. `required <= enumerated` over thirteen literal paths is DELETED, not extended -- that shape was rejected at EVAL-RERUN-DF-01 and again at ARM_MODULE_PREFIXES, and is worse here because the literal must be edited by whoever just forgot to register the instrument. [registry.enumeration] declares a scope and the members are derived by walking the tree. SM-GM-I3 flips SURVIVES -> DIES. The check measures a tree it is HANDED, never the one it lives in, because SM-01 found the gap-mutant runner detecting itself. Findings SM-03-DF-01..03 filed, none fixed, budget 5 spent 3. The load-bearing one: demonstrate.py judges an EXIT CODE where run_gap_mutants.py one directory over compares FAILURE SETS against a pristine baseline, which is why the last two tripwires still cannot be demonstrated -- one layer of "the reason was about the harness" was peeled off and another was found underneath.

entries.narrative: SM-04 fixed four defects in the eval scorecard and NOTHING ELSE, and bumped the card to `scorecard_version 3`. THE ANCHORS DID NOT MOVE: `anchors_digest` is `sha256:eeccf4576bc6fd85` at versions 1, 2 and 3 alike, `check` recomputes it from the file on every run, and a test asserts the literal. D2, D4 and D5 are all still on the card. 1. THE DIGEST WAS BLIND TO WHAT REACHED A JUDGE. `sha256:e33638087c4191da` at six commits spanning 9,705 to 19,503 bytes -- one hash over a file that doubled, every version of which the dispatch told the judges to read in full. The fix is not a wider hash: it is that "what reaches a judge" now HAS a definition. `served_rubric` renders the judge-facing rubric from parsed structure only, `serve` emits it, `scaffold` writes the same bytes into `scorecard.md`, and every card records `served_digest` over exactly those bytes. Defects 1 and 2 are one fix, because you cannot digest what reaches a judge until you have decided what reaches a judge. 2. A JUDGE WAS SERVED THE FINDING THEY WERE THE INSTRUMENT FOR. The mechanism is the whitelist -- ` later editor adds are outside the renderer by construction, so a new section does not reach a judge by default. The refusal is the backstop. It found two REAL leaks, and the second is the one nobody had seen: `FI-03-DF-02` and `FI-06-DF-04` both located the contamination in the rubric FILE, and neither looked at `_skeleton_md`, which told every version 2 judge "D1, D4 and D5 all moved on unchanged input" IN THEIR OWN CARD. 6 of 6 version 2 cards. Filed as `SM-04-DF-01`; two independent adversarial channels named the right paragraph and the wrong file. 3. D5's ANCHOR IS AMBIGUOUS AND STAYS THAT WAY, VISIBLY. The anchor is untouched. Version 3 does to it what version 2 did to practice: record the choice, never mandate it. It fired once in this round and did exactly what it says -- one judge scored 3 with `anchor_reading: measured` and wrote that under `disclosure` the same lines are a 4. The judge who did NOT reach the field found the sharper thing: the two readings only diverge once anchor 3 holds, so the rule as shipped over-collects, which is the safe direction. 4. `total` IS GONE, and the removal is PRICED rather than assumed. `removal_is_a_delta_rule`: SM-01 seeded for two cuts and neither is this one, so the gap was seeded here, both sides measured in one run. The measurement that decides the earn-its-keep question: a gap mutant can report that a removal cost something only if EVERY detector that killed it is one the removal deletes. refinement.detail:
SEARCHED, FOUND NONE, AND THE ONE REFINEMENT CONSIDERED WAS DECLINED ON RECORD. RD-05 adds no TLA+ representation at all: the model is unchanged and the complexity delta is zero against RD-04. The tag is an eval-harness surface under examples/validation/, which the plan's representation_scope keeps out of the model, and it refuses nothing about any artifact.
THE REFINEMENT CONSIDERED AND DECLINED: caching the derived tag per subject so that `audit` does not shell out to the complexity instrument eleven times per run (~1.1 s). It would remove the only expensive step in R-H1's third clause. It is declined because RE-DERIVATION IS THE ANTI-STALENESS PROPERTY -- a cached authority row is exactly the stale row the clause exists to catch, and R-H5's history is an unnumbered rule with no check that `audit` rejected within the minute. Priced instead, as RD-05-DF-05.
A second was considered and declined harder: making the derivation read a previously written complexity JSON instead of invoking the instrument. That would also have removed the file from two tripwires' reach -- which is the demonstrated blind spot at tests/test_instrument_demonstrations.py::test_the_blind_spot_is_real, and using it deliberately would be defeating a tripwire rather than satisfying one.

entries.narrative:
specs/results/scorecards/reading-discipline/GOAL-tags-earn-their-place/RD-05/RESULT.md is the narrative ledger, and references/architecture_tags.md §13 is the design side of it.
WHAT WAS ADDED, AND WHY IT IS NOT PROGRAM COMPLEXITY. One eval-harness module (`examples/validation/scorecards/architecture_tags.py`), one declared-scope registry (`subjects.toml`), two commands on `score_tools.py`, a third clause on R-H1 that `audit` executes, and 32 tests. NO TLA+, no adapters, no test-graph node, and no gate: the exit code of every tag command is 0 by construction and a test asserts it. The model delta is ZERO and was expected to be (`model_delta_expectation: none expected` in the plan).
WHAT IT BUYS. Architecture becomes a third comparability axis, so an architecture-scoped claim can be refused the way an example-scoped one is -- but ONLY on the one (dimension, value-pair) cell the record demonstrates, D3 on ab_quota_ledger, in one judge tier. On D1, D2, D4 and D5 a "different architecture" objection is not available at all.
THE MEASURED ALTERNATIVE THAT MATTERS. The epic owner's §6b ruling licensed deriving the tag from complexity figures; RD-05 could have taken the exemption the ruling explicitly forbade, or moved the file out of the scan's reach. Both were rejected and the INVARIANT'S STATEMENT was corrected instead: it now forbids a figure REFUSING (raise / assert / exit / a branch whose arm does one), and reports observation. Measured effect, archive tree, no homes: the one failure RD-04 escalated goes green and the like-for-like diff against the parent is exactly one member removed, nothing added.
THE FINDING THE CORE CANNOT EXPRESS. RD-05-DF-01: the scan that produced the escalation was firing on a subprocess exit status, not on a figure, because taint does not cross a function boundary -- so the clauses §9.9 escalated were never visible to it, and an empty refusal list is not coverage. The repair re-classifies what the scan sees and does not widen it.

entries.narrative: specs/results/scorecards/reading-discipline/GOAL-product-round/RD-03/RESULT.md RD-03 is the EVALUATION ticket closing `reading-discipline`. It decides all four epic goals and it changes no program behaviour: 17 findings filed, ZERO fixed, no artifact tree touched, and the one suite failure the round caused left red rather than repaired. WHAT WAS MEASURED. Twelve blind judges at two model tiers scored RD-06's six subjects as three before/after pairs, 24 cards. D2 anchor 3 became reachable on the product side for the first time: eight judges saw a code change and eight awarded it; four saw none and four refused it; NOT ONE split on the size of the delta. `D2 = 2`, constant on 35 of 35 cards of `ab_quota_ledger` and the figure an entire predecessor epic was opened on, is retired -- not because the card changed (the served rubric digest is byte-identical) but because a subject was finally given a before. WHAT IT COST TO BELIEVE. Eight judges independently reported that the complexity descriptor cannot see what they scored (19 of 21 axes byte-identical on one pair; `branch_points` moving the wrong way on the other). D2 split by judge tier for the first time in the record, downstream of a D4 split that is a disagreement about what "model-derived" means. The sweep count moved 22 figures to REFUTED without a document changing, because the card population grew. THE FOUR GOALS: `GOAL-product-round` decided with three verdicts and a reason each (Q1 NOT ANSWERABLE on this fixture and now measured to be so; Q2 NO for the prompt, YES for the revision pass; Q3 YES, on instrument reach rather than code quality). `GOAL-scope-loss-catchable` MET, reported with all three known bounds on its instrument. `GOAL-tags-earn-their-place` MET on deletion and not on admission, with the `opus`-only limit now CLOSED and the closure's own bound stated. `GOAL-apparatus-priced` CONFIRMED LOAD-BEARING on re-run evidence, with the pricing instrument shown entailed at 0 of 10. 7 of the 17 findings are PRODUCT SURFACE, against zero in each of the last two epics. Full reasoning, every rejection, and the sealed predictions scored (4 of 14 falsified) are in the RESULT.md named above.

entries.narrative: CL-02 -- A PRICE STOPS BEING ENTAILED BY THE SHAPE OF THE REMOVAL. THE HEADLINE IS THE UNINTERESTING DIRECTION AND IT IS REPORTED FIRST: NOTHING CAME BACK NON-ZERO. Every historical removal with a published before-table was re-priced with the corrected instrument, on the entailed side and the measured side, and the total is 0 priced results. `RM-01-RF-1` is still PRICED and is still the only price this project has. WHAT WAS BROKEN. `RM-05` withdrew `RM-03`'s "first PRICED removal in this project's history": the round's own control -- `is_control` true, `removed_by` "nothing", `gap` "NONE, on purpose" -- returned the headline verdict, and that row was missing from the four-row output the report printed as three. For every fault all of whose killing nodes lie in a file the removal deletes, `ENTAILED-SURVIVES` follows from `git show` alone and no other verdict is reachable. Both halves were reproduced at 10cf11a BEFORE a line was changed and the transcripts are in the tree (`specs/results/scorecards/close-the-loop/GOAL-price-means-something/parent-10cf11a-same-commands.txt`). THREE CHANGES, ALL IN ONE NON-PRODUCT FILE. (1) `EXTINCT`: a fault whose habitat the removal deleted has no post-removal artifact to be seeded into, so there is nothing left to detect. It is NOT a price and NOT a zero -- it is a refusal to measure, and the capability such a removal costs is measured by nothing here. The wording is the repository's own, from `residual_faults.toml`'s `[[not_seedable]]` row, which stated the distinction and never computed it. (2) A declared control is `CONTROL-EXCLUDED` in every mode and can never be a priced result -- but it is still PRINTED, in its own block outside every denominator, because RM-05's defect was a control row GOING MISSING, and a tidier table would reproduce it exactly. (3) `--head` is resolved with `git rev-parse --verify` before any verdict is computed; an unresolvable head used to make every killing node look deleted and price the whole table at exit 0. THE CARE THAT KEPT IT HONEST. Habitat is read from the EDIT OPS, never from the declared path list. `SM-GM-I3` edits `scripts/gap_probe_instrument.py` with `op = "add_file"`, and that path is absent at `bf0fb29` BECAUSE THE MUTANT CREATES IT. A path-list rule would have called it extinct and made SM-03's removal look cheaper on a bookkeeping detail. Guarded by a test. MEASURED ALTERNATIVES REJECTED. Rendering `EXTINCT` as `FREE` or counting it as a zero -- it asserts safety on evidence that does not exist. Dropping control rows from the table -- that IS the RM-05 failure. Fixing `RM-05-DF-02` (`price` returns PRICED over an all-INERT after-table; still reproduces, filed as CL-02-DF-02) -- that change can only turn a PRICED into a refusal, which makes past removals look CHEAPER, and making it in the commit that reports a re-priced history is the tuning this goal fails a ticket for. Pinning `RECORD`'s floating `head = "HEAD"` (filed as CL-02-DF-01) -- it moves `audit`'s ten sealed rows in the same commit as the measurement taken against them. NOTHING WAS ADJUSTED AFTER A RESULT WAS SEEN. BOUNDS THAT TRAVEL WITH THE VERDICTS. `EXTINCT` is file-granular: a mechanism RENAMED rather than deleted reads EXTINCT and is not extinct. It is an upper bound on extinction exactly as `ENTAILED-SURVIVES` is an upper bound on the price. Both bounds are in the row's own `why`. NO NEW GATES. Nothing in the repository invokes the pricer, no close path consults it, and its exit code refuses nothing about the design. The served surface is untouched at 6,319 bytes and 9 rungs -- the card was not edited. SUITE, WITH ITS TREE. 2 failed, 1492 passed in the real checkout wt-epic-close-the-loop-CL-02 at feature/CL-02 (NOT a `git archive` tree). The two are the inherited deliberate reds, neither repaired: RM-06-DF-01, and `test_nothing_in_the_repository_invokes_the_pricer`, which now names TWO narrative documents because this epic's charter mentions the pricer. It was not allow-listed and not deepened -- no new mention was added outside `specs/`. `denominator_rule`: 1479 -> 1494 collected, failures unchanged; +11 is the numerator rising (this ticket's tests, all of which fail at 10cf11a), +4 is the denominator rising through `test_spec_yaml_valid.py`'s parametrisation over the ticket workspace `open ticket CL-02` scaffolded. No test was removed, skipped or weakened. R1. entries.narrative: CL-03, wave 2. THE MODEL DID NOT MOVE AND WAS NOT MEANT TO.
