refinement.detail: Searched, found none, and the reason is structural rather than a shrug. CL-04 is `role: evaluation` with `model_delta_expectation: none expected`. It changed no TLA+ model, no adapter, no generated code and no shipped instrument; `specs/tickets/CL-04/current` and `.../desired` are byte-identical, and the close-out itself measured `delta: direction=zero (vs CL-03)`. Its entire product is three sealed measurement documents, six ledger findings and a NEXT-EPIC section. A refinement recommendation here would have to be a recommendation about a model this ticket did not touch, derived during a round whose declared job is to MEASURE that model's surroundings and fix nothing. Proposing one would be the `measurement_rule` violation the epic files findings about: a round that changes the thing in the commit that reports on it. Two of CL-04's own findings -- `CL-04-DF-01` and `CL-04-DF-06` -- name concrete repairs to shipped instruments and were deliberately NOT applied for exactly this reason, with the repair written into `suggested_fix` so the next round inherits it. The bound is stated: no TLC run was performed by this ticket, so `measured` is false and nothing here is offered as a measured refinement claim. The reported bound of 1,111,320 is over the 1,000,000 cap and is INHERITED from CL-03 unchanged -- it is a lower bound over 7 of 9 resolved variables, it moved zero this ticket, and CL-04 is not the round that may move it.

entries.narrative: FULL RECORD: `specs/results/scorecards/close-the-loop/CL-04/RESULT.md`. PREDICTIONS, sealed 2026-08-11T21:00:12Z in commit `ab73164` BEFORE any measurement and before either blind agent was dispatched: `specs/results/scorecards/close-the-loop/CL-04/PREDICTIONS-CL-04.md`. WHAT THIS TICKET DECIDED. All three epic goals. `GOAL-change-rule-runnable`: MET, and "a stranger can run it" is now DEMONSTRATED rather than plausible -- a stranger's NEXT bump (5 -> 6, one file, zero Python) produced `2 failed, 1496 passed`, byte-identical to the unmodified tip, and a blind adopter agent bumped the card in its own foreign tree with no configuration at all. But the change rule fails loudly only UPWARDS: `scaffold --card-version 4` at the tip stamps a card `version 4`, serves it version 5's bytes, and `check` reports 0 problems. `GOAL-price-means-something`: MET on every clause, and the instrument still has exactly one price to its name. `GOAL-loop-closes-once`: MET, reproduced from the sealed cards with no judge re-run -- and the closure has NO NEGATIVE CONTROL, which is the next epic's first ticket. THE HEADLINE. The epic's own premise is false. It said the loop "cannot be run by anyone who did not build it"; a blind agent given only the shipped files, forbidden our source, our `specs/`, our tests and our git history, ran it end to end and our D3 caveat fired correctly on an artifact we had never seen. THE SERVED SURFACE: 6,319 -> 6,281 bytes, rungs 9 -> 9. It fell. Not a `git archive` figure; measured in clean detached checkouts named in the RESULT. Suite: 2 failed at both ends, the two inherited deliberate reds, neither repaired. +27 collected across the epic, ALL numerator, decomposed per file; `test_spec_yaml_valid.py` did not move because both trees are clean checkouts rather than ticket workspaces. COST, WITH ITS BASIS NAMED as the standing rule requires: the harness's `subagent_tokens` field, composition undocumented -- 102,034 for the adopter probe (1 finding, 0.98/100k) and 84,214 for the census (0 findings, 0.00/100k), 186,248 across both blind channels for 1 finding, 0.54/100k. NOT comparable to RD-03's 1.14, which used a different and named basis. The numerator was NOT budget-capped: six filed against a budget of five, the sixth escalated, nothing dropped. The three tickets that did the epic's work recorded no token count at all, the second consecutive epic to record none, filed as `CL-04-DF-02`. FINDINGS FILED, NONE FIXED: `CL-04-DF-01` through `CL-04-DF-06`. Two of them name repairs to shipped instruments that were deliberately not applied. THE ALARM DID NOT FIRE -- three of eleven predictions were falsified -- and the RESULT says why that is not self-congratulation: six of the eleven only predicted that the predecessors' reports would reproduce, and two of the three predictions carrying a real mechanism were the ones that broke.

entries.narrative:
specs/results/scorecards/score-drives-validation/GOAL-scored-at-goal-time/SV-06/RESULT.md is the evidence ledger and `references/goal_score_wiring.md` is the design.
WHAT WAS MEASURED. Over every `ticket_plan.yaml` on disk at `a527305`, live and sealed: 27 distinct epic goals, 12 of which name a scorecard dimension in prose, and ZERO whose `baseline.evidence` points at a sealed `scorecard.json` -- against 87 sealed cards in the record. The epic's own baseline says "NO GOAL HAS EVER BEEN KEYED TO A DIMENSION"; that clause is false (SV-06-DF-01) and the true gap is sharper: a goal here has DESCRIBED a score twelve times and has never BEEN one.
THE MEASURED ALTERNATIVE, RUN AND REJECTED. An optional `scored_by:` block on `epic_goals[]` plus a `score_signal:` on the ticket-goal link was added to a scratch copy of this epic's plan and put through `git-epic-workflow/scripts/validate_epic_plan.py`: exit 0, byte-identical message, zero lines of Python changed, because the plan schema reads named fields and ignores unknown ones. It is REJECTED anyway -- every field is already sayable in `harness`, `metric` and `baseline.evidence`, and `dimension:` would export an index into one project's rubric into a schema three skills share. Cheap to add is not a reason to add. The experiment is sealed at validator-experiment/ because it is the argument AGAINST the field, and because its other half is the absence guarantee: a plan with no scoring block validates today, unchanged, and will validate identically after SV-07.
ALSO REJECTED: scoring at ticket start or ticket close (cost, rubric noise exceeding one ticket's movement, and R-H1/R-H2 comparability against a mid-epic tree); any new check or gate, including a check that a judged goal carries a card baseline (`no_new_gates_rule` -- 0 of 27 argues for a sentence, not a checker); a `--goal` flag on `score_tools.py` or any `tla-spec-dev` path that reads a plan, which would invert the dependency and make the card a participant in the goal process rather than an instrument it names; and a shared "judged instrument" reference page in any skill, which would be a seventh file in a surface this ticket had just finished counting.
WHAT THE CORE CANNOT EXPRESS. A THIRD suite red is inherited and the epic lists only two. `tests/test_card_has_one_home.py::test_only_the_card_states_a_dimension_an_anchor_or_a_scoring_rule` fails on four lines in `SCORE-DRIVES-VALIDATION-EPIC.md` and `specs/desired_program_model/ticket_plan.yaml` -- the only two files `a527305` touched, in the same document that says "Two reds are inherited deliberately". Demonstrated inherited, not caused: with this ticket's page, evidence tree and findings all removed, the failure is identical, and SV-06's own design page appears nowhere in the offender list. NOT FILED -- the finding budget of 5 is spent and none of the five is blocking; escalated in RESULT.md section 7 and the ticket report, per RM-02's precedent. NOT REPAIRED -- both files are outside this ticket's implementation scope and silently repairing an inherited red is forbidden.
BYTE COST: zero. Nothing here touches `references/eval_scorecard.md`, so `serve` stays 6,281 bytes and 9 rungs, and the SV-07 hand-off creates no anchor -- four prose edits across three skill files and one free-text plan convention. NO SKILL WAS EDITED by this ticket and `skill-manager sync` was never run.

SV-06's 0-of-27 is a string test; this ticket resolved every `baseline.evidence` against the filesystem and asked the question the evaluation ticket actually has to answer -- can you OPEN the card that produced the number? Of 27 distinct goals, 18 name a judged instrument and 0 OF THOSE 18 have a baseline that can be opened: 8 cite a directory, 8 cite a document, 1 cites a path that does not resolve at all, and 1 is pure prose. 87 sealed cards sit uncited. The judged denominator is 18, not 27 (SV-03-DF-02, `denominator_rule`) -- the correction makes the compliance rate worse. R1, ON A REAL EPIC PLAN. `GOAL-loop-reaches-the-program` in this epic's own live plan cites `specs/results/scorecards/close-the-loop/`, which contains ZERO scorecard.json files -- the CL-03 cards are in two sibling directories. A SECOND FAILING INPUT, AIMED AT THE PROPOSAL ITSELF. SV-06's verbatim wording for edit 2 asks for "the path to the SINGLE sealed card". Two judged goals here have baselines that are figures over a POPULATION of cards -- including `GOAL-D2-can-move`, the goal SV-06 holds up as the best of its kind -- so the sentence is unsatisfiable for them. It has no failing exit path at all, nothing in `scripts/` reads it, and two tests assert both. The thing a checker would gate is the epic owner's prose about their own baseline. COST. `serve | wc -c` is 6,281 bytes at 9 rungs and digest sha256:2d7d4a0506d9b259 before and after -- unchanged, because nothing here touches `references/eval_scorecard.md`. The copy is the tool's own documented remedy. (3) Reusing the two version 4 cards that already exist on these bytes: a different round, packet and dispatch, so the card version would not have been the only mover. They are recorded as a stated prior and averaged with nothing. (4) Running unblinded as CL-03 did: blinding was used anyway -- `subject.name` null, declared boundary withheld -- because it cost nothing and is strictly better.

SUITE, WITH ITS TREE. 2 failed, 1501 passed at 6d895de, reconciled onto epic tip b999d71. The two are exactly the inherited deliberate pair and neither is repaired. THAT TREE IS STALE ON PURPOSE: the epic tip moved four times during this round and 6d895de predates 86a8767, which it was NOT re-measured against, at the epic owner's instruction. denominator_rule: collected 1,498 -> 1,503, and none of the +5 are this ticket's -- they arrive through SV-06 in the reconciliation. THE CLASS CONSUMED. A1 -- the real adapter's one distinguishing property is observed by nothing -- found by four judges across three epics plus two more in CL-03's own round, filed once as RM-05-DF-05, and consumed by nothing for seven epics. It is real: gut FileJournal to a list and the shared 28-case suite passes 28 of 28 through the real wiring while creating zero ledger.txt files against 28 at control. This is its third independent reproduction. THE CARRIER, AND WHY. An adapter conformance suite, examples/validation/ab/tests/test_journal_conformance.py, 14 cases. It exercises both implementations of the LedgerJournal port directly, and every assertion about the durable record is made OUT OF BAND through Path.read_text() on the declared path, never through lines(). A suite that reads the record back through the adapter that wrote it is asking the writer whether it wrote, and gets the same answer from an adapter that touched no filesystem. Not the shared contract suite, which both arms are measured against and which a durability case must fail under the fake wiring; not inside reference_ports/, because the counterfactual depends on the scored scope's bytes not moving; not a diagram, because diagram, mermaid, UML, C4 and .svg appear in 0 of 87 sealed cards. The suite is justified by a seven-mutant matrix sealed before the round, three of whose mutants are lifted unchanged from the fixture's own seeded_faults.toml so it is not measured only against faults its author invented. M1 through M4 survive the shared suite 56 of 56 under both wirings and die under the new file. Two arms judged concurrently, blind to each other and to which arm they hold: a control packet byte-identical to CL-03's, and the same plus one added file, both verified with diff -r. D3 reads 3, 3 on the control and 4, 4 on the treatment; D2 reads 2 on all four with nothing contested. All four judges independently reproduced the harvested class, and the score separates exactly on whether an out-of-band observer is present. The control arm exists because the predecessor round's own two passes scored D2 = 2 and D2 = 0 on byte-identical bytes, which is too much spread to attribute a one-round difference to a treatment. The model did not move because the thing measured is not in the model. What CA-01 measured is what the HARNESS puts in a dispatched agent's context before it reads anything, and no TLA+ variable can see that.
THE MEASUREMENT. Four agents dispatched, asked only to report their own pre-read context verbatim and what they rejected. Three of four received the operator's `MEMORY.md` in full plus the five most recent commit subject lines before any tool call; one (`Explore`) received neither. That CORRECTS `SV-05-DF-02`'s "4 of 4" to a tier and narrows a published figure. The half that survives is the half that matters: it reaches the agent types this project actually uses for judges.
MEASURED ALTERNATIVES, each refused with a reason. (1) Ship `Explore` as the blinding mechanism. Cheapest result available; would
    have closed this ticket with ZERO new apparatus and no `GOAL-apparatus-cut`
    regression. Refused: one observation, one harness version, undocumented
    behaviour, and the `Explore` arm shared the leaking session so cwd does not
    explain it. `SV-05-DF-01` is this project's own precedent for what that bet
    costs -- a version flag that served the wrong card and was accepted.
(2) `claude --bare`. The harness's own switch, documented to skip auto-memory,
    hooks and CLAUDE.md discovery in one flag -- strictly better than what
    shipped. Unusable here: it forces `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper`
    and never reads OAuth or the keychain, and no key is set. `CA-01-DF-02`.
(3) `--safe-mode`. Plausible, keeps normal auth, NOT documented to disable
    auto-memory. Not measured, so nothing is claimed in either direction.
(4) Write the instrument in shell. The `GOAL-apparatus-cut` command counts
    `*.py`, so shell would have cost zero MEASURED lines for identical
    function. Refused as gaming the denominator; written in Python and priced.
(5) Suppress the SessionStart hook to clear `CA-01-DF-01`. Would have turned a
    blocking finding into a clean pass in one settings change. Refused: it is
    the operator's machine, the charter forbids applying such a change, and it
    was never measured to work.

THE FINDING THE CORE CANNOT CARRY. Blindness to the operator's CONCLUSIONS is achievable and is proven on real subjects -- `check` REFUSES a fresh repo-rooted `claude -p` (26 indicators) and a judge-shaped subagent (25), and PASSES a neutral cell. Blindness to the project's IDENTITY is NOT achievable with this harness: the arm that passed still received the SessionStart hook naming `spec-double-compiler` and `test-graph`, and the skill listing describing the TLA+ spec-double pipeline. Filed `CA-01-DF-01`, BLOCKING, because it decides what `CA-08` may call its rounds.
R1 EARNED ITS KEEP HERE. Run against its first real subject the instrument derived ZERO memory needles -- the ticket worktree has no memory slug while the primary checkout it branched from has all 19 files -- and would have returned a pass carried only by literal block labels. Fixed with `--memory` and a `WEAK PASS` warning, and written up rather than quietly corrected.

THIS TICKET MOVES GOAL-apparatus-cut THE WRONG WAY, by 169 lines, and it is the third epic running in which a ticket called a simplification came out net-additive -- which is RM-03-DF-03's structural point arriving on schedule. ZERO DELETIONS, SO CLAUSE (b) IS SATISFIED VACUOUSLY AND SHOULD BE READ THAT WAY. entries.narrative:
FULL RECORD: specs/results/scorecards/cut-the-apparatus/CA-04/PRICE-TABLE.md (the cut, its price, what the model can no longer express, and what was rejected) and .../descriptor-comparison.md (the before/after basis).
WHAT THIS CLOSE IS. CA-04 removed oracle 4, the mutation kill test, and with it the last hard static gate in this repository. The finding is RM-03-DF-05, which identified this exact cut, declined it because it was a model delta its own ticket forbade, and whose suggested_fix asked for "its own ticket against the CLI model". Removed: the kill_test variable, the RunKillTest action and the KillTestVerdictRequiresBudgets invariant; RunKillTestAdapter and its binding; kill_rate_floor, the mutation_write port and RunKillTest's port row; three kill_mutants.toml catalogues; three spec-unit adapter tests; scripts/run_kill_test.py; tests/test_kill_test.py; and the `run kill-test` subcommand. scripts/ -1,105 lines. The card is untouched at 6,281 bytes.
THE DECREASE IS LICENSED, AND IT WAS NOT LICENSED WHEN THIS CLOSE WAS FIRST ATTEMPTED. The first attempt was REFUSED by this ledger -- "complexity decreased but the validated-refactor basis is UNVERIFIED ... absent evidence is not passing evidence" -- because CA-04 had run no TLC on either side. That refusal was correct and is kept at .../close-refusal.txt. The basis above was then measured rather than argued around: TLC green on both models, the before-model reconstructed from the branch point and verified by sha AND by reproducing the 563,963-state figure the repository had already recorded for it.
WHAT THE MODEL CAN NO LONGER EXPRESS, which is the price and is not softened: nothing validates the representation against the PROGRAM. The model's own comment said kill_test was "the only one of the four [oracles] that validates the representation against the PROGRAM rather than against itself ... none of them can tell a faithful model from a vacuous one. This can." The cost caps have lost their matching value floor; coverage can drift behind the model silently; and compare_reports, the mechanism separating a legitimate simplification from a disguised deletion, is gone -- in a cutting epic. A green tlc_after is therefore WEAKER evidence here than for an ordinary refactor: it certifies the remaining model's self-consistency, which is precisely the property the kill test existed because TLC could not check.
THE MEASUREMENT THAT GOT WORSE, recorded because the flattering version was already written down and had to be withdrawn: the declared bound fell 1,111,320 -> 277,830, and an earlier draft of the price table called that "now under the declared max_state_space_bound for the first time". It is not. `comparable_to_cap` returns None rather than True for an incomplete bound at or under the cap, and the scanner's advisory changed from `state_space_bound` to `state_space_bound_partial`, "INCOMPLETE and CANNOT be compared". The model did not become compliant; it became unmeasurable against the cap. The refinement search above names the move that would repair that.
TWO ORDERED DELETIONS WERE REFUSED, both on the record rather than on taste. kill_test.py could not be deleted whole: five in-repo consumers import its catalogue parser and suppression scanner, including examples/validation/ab/eval/run_controls.py at MODULE SCOPE, which is the driver RD-03 used for the model-derived columns whose zero unique kills is a load-bearing disproof. Measured by parking the file. The oracle-4 half was cut (839 of 1,149 lines) and the 310-line parser/scanner retained; three of those five consumers were found by the reviewer, not by me. candidate_note_bar.py was not deleted at all: SV-06-DF-04 does not say what four documents say it says, "the shortest test asserts nothing imports it" is false (it asserts the card is still 6,281 bytes, the only such assertion in the repository), it is the named reproduction of the open SV-07-DF-01, and instruments.toml declares it with two demonstration nodes. CA-04-DF-01 through -03.
THE MOST TRANSFERABLE RESULT IS CA-04-DF-06 AND IT GENERALISES BEYOND THIS CUT. The epic's REQUIRED loader check greps deleted PATHS, so it is structurally blind to deleted INTERFACES -- CLI subcommands, exported symbols, manifest keys and TOML sections have no basename to grep for. Every cutting ticket in this programme runs a check that cannot see the interfaces it retires, and shipped adopter-facing instructions rot with nothing going red. Demonstrated on this ticket's own cut: SKILL.md:1167 and :1174 still tell adopters to run `tla-spec-dev run kill-test`, which now answers "invalid choice". CA-04-DF-08 is the same defect from the other end -- the validation matrix handed to all eight tickets names `tla-spec-dev run tlc`, and there is no such subcommand.
AND THE FINDING THIS LEDGER PRODUCED ABOUT ITSELF: CA-04-DF-07. A hard gate refused a real promotion, on substance, and it was right. Its decrease clause had been DORMANT for the whole epic -- CA-02 and CA-03 both left validated_refactor entirely at its template default and closed cleanly, because neither changed the model -- and it fired on the first ticket that reached it. Complying with it caught two errors in this ticket's own reporting that nothing else had asked for. The charter carries "static gates catch nothing -- seven epics, zero bugs" among four disproven claims and uses it to forbid adding gates; with CA-03-DF-05's record-checks and CA-05's registry tripwire, that sentence is in serious trouble. This is not a licence to add a gate, and CA-04 added none -- it removed the last hard one.
Eight findings filed against a declared budget of five, all disposed; the overrun is recorded as an overrun. Suite 8 failed / 1466 passed on the merged tip: six pre-existing at CA-03's tip and two this ticket's, both declared, both outside its scope, none repaired.

entries.narrative:
CA-05 -- the disposition requirement. Full working: specs/results/scorecards/cut-the-apparatus/GOAL-consumption-obligatory/CA-05/refusal.md and .../harvest-recount.md; the rule itself is references/consumption.md.
WHAT SHIPPED. An epic may not close while a finding it filed is undisposed: D1 a disposition that is not `open`, D2 a note on a terminal disposition, D3 a named successor on a deferral. Vocabulary closed on purpose. NOT A GATE ON ANYONE'S CODE -- it reads one file in this repository and reports on this project's own epics; seven epics of static checking caught zero bugs and this epic adds none.
R1, DISCHARGED ON REAL INPUT. Run against the sealed 225-row ledger it REFUSES cut-the-apparatus at 10 of 15 rows open -- this epic, its own close-out, not a fixture -- while ACCEPTING falsifiable-instruments (30/30) and subtract-to-measure (30/30), and refusing ports-as-adapters on 2 of 28 rows under D2 alone. Two real epics pass, six refuse, the refusals differ in size and clause, and one real slice (--ticket CA-05) passes inside a refused epic. A rule that refuses everything is a constant, not a measurement -- the mirror of harvest class D1 -- so the discrimination was demonstrated separately rather than assumed.
THE FINDING, AND IT IS NOT THE ONE THE TICKET WAS SENT TO GET. The premise "consumption is 1 of 38 because nothing requires it" is half wrong. A disposition practice EXISTED, ran three consecutive epics, routed 83 findings into named successors -- including five purpose-built carry-forward issues, #144-#148, still open today -- and STOPPED DEAD on 2026-08-08 with no discussion in any record. And the same four epics are missing from SELF-IMPROVEMENT.md, whose sections end at SM-05 on 2026-08-07: the correlation is exact across all eight epics in both directions. Both registers lapsed at the same commit because nothing reported on either. CA-05-DF-01.
THE REGISTER. 38 verified before it was changed, then SV-01-DF-05's three unswept classes appended as G1-G3. Per denominator_rule: THE DENOMINATOR ROSE 38 -> 41, THE NUMERATOR DID NOT MOVE, 2.6% -> 2.4%; the rate fell on a bookkeeping repair, nothing regressed. 41 IS A FLOOR -- the sweep read 83 cards, the tree holds 95, twelve are unswept (CA-05-DF-04). And three of the four classes named by a ledger row are this project catching ITSELF committing the class; only A1 was consumed.
MEASURED ALTERNATIVES, REJECTED. (1) A pure-prose requirement with a grep, which the charter prefers -- rejected because grep cannot scope to an epic or check the D2/D3 grammar, and the "demonstrated refusal" R1 demands would not have been reproducible. (2) Hiding the instrument in tests/, where GOAL-apparatus-cut does not count it -- rejected as metric-dodging; it sits in scripts/ and is priced at +133 lines. (3) Retro-classifying `channel` on the 210 pre-existing rows -- rejected because assigning a channel from somebody else's prose is exactly the hand classification the field exists to end, and in bulk it would manufacture a clean history nobody measured. (4) Building the consumption half of the check -- rejected as apparatus measuring apparatus, and DECLARED as the instrument's known blindness instead (CA-05-DF-03): a row can satisfy all three clauses by being carried to an issue that closes unread, and falsifiable-instruments passes on exactly that shape.
PRICE. scripts/ 27,652 -> 27,785 (+133, scripts/disposition.py). tests/ +119. examples/validation/ 16,129, UNCHANGED. Card 6,281 bytes, sha256:2d7d4a0506d9b259, UNCHANGED -- clause (c) of GOAL-apparatus-cut holds. The surfaces are reported separately and never combined with the card.

The epic ships documentation and prompts: `references/bug_attribution.md` (the four record kinds -- CATCH, REACH, BLIND, PRICE), the two surfaces that ask for them at ticket close-out and workflow close, `prompts/regression_architecture.md`, and AT-04's clause-by-clause evaluation of six goals. MODEL DELTA IS ZERO AND THAT IS THE TICKET: no TLA+ action, variable or invariant was added, removed or changed, and `specs/current` was byte-identical to `specs/desired_program_model` on every semantic file at close. Six goals MET; one clause of GOAL-the-record-says-what-caught-it is DESIGNED, NOT APPLIED, because the 364-row ledger whose 27 out-of-vocabulary rows it would dispose lives on epic/stabilize-substrate and arrives with #296 -- stated in AT-04's RESULT.md as the epic's single largest limitation rather than worked around.
notes: NOTE: TLC reports incomplete; comparison skipped.

coverage audit (MF-026) is `not_run`: audit has not been run for this scope. RECORDED, NOT REFUSED (2026-08-04). The four oracles check fidelity of what is modeled and are bounded to it; unmodeled surface is invisible to all of them while they report green, and this is the only sweep that looks at it. Run `prompts/coverage_audit.md` if you want that read on this scope.
